These documents each address this:

How to chill, freeze and defrost food safely (Food Standards Agency, 2017):
- Your fridge should be set between 0 and 5°C. [3]
- Your fridge should be set between 0 and 5°C. [4]
- Leftovers should be eaten within 48 hours or frozen if they cannot be eaten sooner. [3]

Kitchen Companion: Your Safe Food Handbook (U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food Safety and Inspection Service, 2015):
- Cold food should be kept at 40 °F (4.44 °C) or below. [5]

Cold Food Storage Chart (FoodSafety.gov (U.S. Department of Health and Human Services), 2023):
- Leftovers can be kept in the fridge for 3 to 4 days. [6]
- Soups and stews with vegetables or meat added can be kept in the fridge for 3 to 4 days. [6]
- Cooked meat or poultry leftovers can be kept in the fridge for 3 to 4 days. [6]
- Pizza leftovers can be kept in the fridge for 3 to 4 days. [6]

From How to chill, freeze and defrost food safely (Food Standards Agency, 2017):
- Defrost meat in the fridge using a container big enough to catch any drips, ensuring it is fully thawed before cooking [1]
- The safest way to defrost meat is in the fridge overnight so it never enters the 8‑63 °C danger zone [6]
